content.value_statement: Poor error handling hides failures, confuses users, and slows production debugging. This skill guides reviews toward clear messages, recovery paths, and useful logs.
actual_capabilities: Reviews try and catch blocks for empty catches, bad scope, cleanup, and missing context.
Checks API and network error handling for retries, fallbacks, and status-aware messages.
Evaluates user-facing error messages for clarity, next steps, and privacy.
Flags stack trace exposure and technical details in API responses.
Guides mentors with review questions for junior developers.
limitations: Provides review guidance only; it does not run code or verify production behavior.
Examples focus mainly on JavaScript, TypeScript, React, forms, and API flows.
Retry guidance is general and does not replace service-specific resilience design.
Project logging standards may be needed for final implementation choices.

use_cases.title: Review Form Failures
use_cases.description: Check form submission flows for helpful validation, loading cleanup, and retry guidance.

use_cases.title: Harden API Errors
use_cases.description: Review API responses so internal details stay private and clients receive useful messages.

use_cases.title: Coach Junior Reviews
use_cases.description: Use focused questions to help developers reason about error scope, logging, and recovery.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Catch Block
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small error handling change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this try and catch block. Identify empty catches, unclear user messages, missing cleanup, and missing debug context.

prompt_templates.title: Review API Error Responses
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of server or client API behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API error flow. Check whether it leaks technical details, logs useful context, and returns actionable messages.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Async Recovery
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of network or background operations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this async operation. Evaluate retry behavior, fallback values, loading states, and when errors should propagate.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Failure Path
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across user experience, observability, and resilience.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature failure path end to end. Prioritize user impact, privacy, logging quality, cleanup, retries, and graceful degradation.

output_examples.input: A form submission catches errors but leaves the loading spinner active.
output_examples.output: Finding: The failure path does not reset loading. Recommendation: Always run cleanup and show a retry message.

output_examples.input: An API endpoint returns exception details and a stack trace to the client.
output_examples.output: Finding: The response exposes internal details. Recommendation: Log diagnostics server-side and return a generic user message.

output_examples.input: A network request retries without telling the user why the screen is waiting.
output_examples.output: Finding: The retry behavior lacks user feedback. Recommendation: Show progress, limit retries, and provide a fallback.

best_practices: Catch errors at the layer that can add context, recover, or present a useful message.
Log diagnostic details for developers while keeping user-facing messages clear and private.
Use cleanup paths so loading, locks, and temporary state are restored after failures.
anti_patterns: Ignoring errors with empty catch blocks or silent null returns.
Showing stack traces, raw exception messages, or jargon to end users.
Retrying failures without limits, feedback, or a fallback plan.

faq.question: What code does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews error handling in try and catch blocks, promises, APIs, forms, network calls, and React error boundaries.

faq.question: Does it execute code?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and examples, but it does not run code or call external services.

faq.question: Can it help with user-facing messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks whether messages are clear, specific, private, and useful for the next user action.

faq.question: Can it replace production monitoring?
faq.answer: No. It can improve logging and error design, but production monitoring still needs project-specific tooling.

faq.question: Which languages are best supported?
faq.answer: The examples focus on JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and API error handling patterns.

faq.question: How should teams use it in reviews?
faq.answer: Use it before merging changes that affect forms, async operations, API responses, or visible error states.
